messages:
alice: FYI — after enabling per-layer int4 with an explicit skipmap for embeddings + lm_head, we bumped p99 by ~6-9% on long-chat traces. I ran a quick profile and saw a lot of kernel switches around mid layers.
ben: can you paste the profile snippet or flamegraph output?
alice: pasted short output: `kernel_selector: picked int4_matmul_v2 for layers 0-11, fp8_gemm for layers 12-18, fallback int8_kern for layer 19-24, then fp8 again`
alice: full perf lines:```
# timeline sample
12:34:56.123 kernel_switch layer=12 reason=quant_profile speedup_est=1.8
12:34:56.223 kernel_switch layer=19 reason=calib_mismatch fallback=fp8_gemm
12:34:56.300 kv_cache: warmup_evictions=14 recompile_ops=3
``` 
carla: interesting — did the layer index change because we excluded embedding/lm_head from quant table? If offsets moved, the selector might think a different op shape applies.
sasha: also +1: kv cache warmup_evictions look suspicious. If the KV mapping changes shape we trigger reprogs which cost latency. Might be interaction of skipmap + batch heuristic.
jie: quick question — were these traces run with `CONTIG_BATCH=1` or default? contiguous batching changes per-layer seqlen distribution and influences kernel selection.
alice: they were default. I'll re-run with `CONTIG_BATCH=1` and post results.
ben: hypothesis: our skipmap removed two entries from quant map, but kernel_selector still uses absolute layer id for choosing quantized kernel. So layer N ends up using kernel tuned for N+2. That matches the fp8 fallback around mid layers.
carla: agree. I remember a similar off-by-offset bug when we excluded lm_head earlier (in a different model). We added an explicit `layer_map_base` in selector. Maybe that wasn't applied here.
sasha: mitigation options: 1) add a skipmap-aware index remap in kernel_selector; 2) emit a metric `quant_index_mismatch` and short-circuit to safe kernel when mismatch probability > 0.15; 3) for immediate canary, force per-layer fallback policy to prefer int8 over fp8 for those mid layers.
alice: +1 to metrics — we need observability before rolling more. Can we get a cheap counter `kernel_selector.layer_offset` and `kv.recompile_count`?
ben: I can add both in ~2hrs. Also propose small unit test: construct dummy model with skipmap and assert selected_kernels per-layer equals expected.
jie: for repro: run `pytest perf/tests/test_skipmap_kernelselector.py::test_layer_offset --profile` and also run long-chat trace with `--batcher=contig` and `--kv-warmup=1000`.
infra-bot: deploy scheduled: canary/quant-skipmap-v2 -> 5% traffic at 1765435600 UTC, auto-rollback on p99 increase > 4% for 30m. :robot_face:
sasha: plan for canary metrics: p50/p90/p99 latency, tokens/s, kernel_switch_count, kv_recompile_count, quant_mismatch_rate. We'll baseline for 1h prior.
carla: small fix idea: add skipmap translation table at model-open time and validate by running a micro-benchmark of 64 warm tokens to confirm kernel selection stability. If mismatch, abort rollout.
alice: I'll run the micro-benchmark and post numbers. If stable, we can go to canary; if not, we'll merge ben's remap patch.
ben: I'll open PR titled `runtime: make kernel_selector skipmap-aware (layer-index remap)` and attach test vectors.
jie: once PR ready I can run CI perf checks and the contig-batcher trace on the CI infra GPU pool.
sasha: sgtm. also add alert for kv.recompile_count > 5/min during canary so SRE gets paged before customers see impact.
alice: thanks all — I'll re-run traces now and paste the micro-benchmark snippet in this thread. :thumbsup:
